objective: Six negative-control runners, scripts/wp111_controls.py through scripts/wp116_controls.py, were written by copying one another and totalled 2,943 lines (#368). #368 measured the result and found exactly ONE shared function byte-identical across its copies, which makes the obvious reading - six duplicates, extract them - the wrong one. The subjects genuinely differ: wp112 and wp114 mutate git history and therefore CLONE, the other four mutate tracked files and therefore COPY, and `fresh` differing from `clone` is the right answer for each caller rather than drift. This package classified every divergence as NEED (a caller genuinely requires it; it survives as a parameter with a live caller on each side) or DRIFT (nothing depended on it) BEFORE extracting anything, put the classification in the new module's own docstring, and extracted only what the classification called common into scripts/control_harness.py. Nothing was resolved by taking the union of two behaviours or the more lenient of them - that is what WP-110 did to four private normalisers, after which the suite passed, four re-run controls passed, and review found eight real divergences that were caught before and missed after. Because each runner is the evidence its own package shipped, adoption was gated per runner on its FULL OUTPUT being byte-identical before and after - every control, the test each trips, every isolation declaration - captured on both sides and diffed, not on the suite staying green. FIX ROUND 1 ADDED THE GUARD THE PACKAGE WAS MISSING. Every parameter had a live caller on each side when the harness was written and review proved it by hand, and nothing kept it true: the next edit can give a parameter a default no caller ever dissents from, at which point the parameter stops expressing a difference and becomes the union of two behaviours with one deleted - WP-110's failure re-entering through the door this package built. tests/test_harness_parameters.py reads scripts/control_harness.py and every scripts/wp*_controls.py with `ast` and refuses a defaulted parameter no runner dissents from. FIX ROUND 1: tests/test_harness_parameters.py GUARDS THE ONE PROPERTY THIS PACKAGE RESTS ON. observations: THE ISSUE'S OWN MEASUREMENT WAS THE FIRST THING RE-MEASURED, AND IT PARTLY DID NOT HOLD. #368's table is the reason this package exists and its `edit` row is not reproducible: six distinct bodies at 10-59 lines against a measured four distinct texts at 8-9 lines. The direction of the finding survives - `edit` HAS drifted, in two ways that matter - but a package that had taken the table on trust would have written a false sentence into its own records on the first line. Re-measure the number the brief hands you, every time.

THE TWO DIFFERENCES IN `edit` ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING AND SEPARATING THEM WAS THE WHOLE JUDGEMENT. The preview width (60 against 70) only ever appears inside an AssertionError that no green run prints; the `newline` argument decides whether `write_text` rewrites EVERY line ending in the file or only the span the mutation touched. On a Windows checkout that is a different file on disk. Unifying the first would have been invisible; unifying the second would have changed what four of the six controls' copies contain. Both are parameters, because output equality does not distinguish them and the bar was output equality.

SIX COPIES OF THE REPORTING LOOP HAD ALREADY DRIFTED INTO TWO WORDINGS AND NOBODY NOTICED. wp111 through wp114 print `DECLARED HOLE: expected the suite to stay GREEN` and warn `the hole has closed; re-derive the limit that declares it`; wp115 and wp116 print neither prefix and warn `re-derive the claim this control stands behind`. Nothing is wrong with either, and a reader comparing two runners' output would reasonably conclude the two branches mean different things. They do not. That is what six copies with no shared definition costs, and it is the concrete argument for this package that is not a line count.

THE COPY-BASED RUNNERS ARE NOT SLOW AND THE BRIEF'S COST ESTIMATE WAS HIGH BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE FOR FOUR OF THE SIX. Measured, the before pass: wp116 1s, wp111 9s, wp115 10s, wp113 22s, wp114 160s, wp112 240s. The two clone-based runners carry essentially all of the cost, because a clone is a clone and their suites are the large ones. Anyone planning the same comparison should budget for the clone-based pair and stop worrying about the other four.

ADDING A FILE TO scripts/ WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE SUITE RATHER THAN ASSUMED SAFE, AND THE ANSWER STOPPED BEING TRUE WHEN THIS PACKAGE ITSELF CHANGED IT. Before the harness was written, `grep -rn "rglob\|iterdir\|glob(" tests/*.py` returned nothing under scripts/ and validate_continuity.py's required-files list is explicit rather than a directory walk, so a new module in scripts/ was inert to both. Fix round 1 falsified the general form of that sentence: the same command now returns tests/test_harness_parameters.py, which globs the runners, so a new file in scripts/ MATCHING `wp*_controls.py` is read by the guard and is not inert - which is the point of the guard. A file in scripts/ that does not match, control_harness.py and build_control_page.py among them, still is. The lesson is not about scripts/: a measurement of what reads a directory is only true until something starts reading it, and this package was the something.

IMPORTING WORKS BECAUSE OF HOW THE RUNNERS ARE INVOKED, AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD. `python scripts/wpNNN_controls.py` puts scripts/ on sys.path as sys.path[0], so `from control_harness import ...` resolves without any package plumbing, any __init__.py or any sys.path manipulation. The harness is imported from the SOURCE checkout in every case; the copies and clones the runners build carry their own inert copy of it and never import it.

FIX ROUND 1'S FINDING, WHICH IS ABOUT THIS PACKAGE AND NOT ABOUT THE HARNESS. The original package proved its property by hand and by review, and then shipped a record saying so - `declared_non_coverage` named the absence of a guard plainly and correctly. A DECLARED HOLE IS NOT THE SAME AS A GUARDED PROPERTY, and declaring one is not a substitute for building the guard when the property is the whole case for the change. The tell was in the record's own words: 'no test that its parameters still have a live caller on each side' sat two lines under 'every parameter has a live caller on each side', which is a claim and its own unguardedness written side by side.

THE ENUMERATION WAS RUN BEFORE THE FIRST EDIT OF FIX ROUND 1, NOT AFTER. Adding a test module falsifies every sentence that says this package adds none, so `grep -rln "adds no test\|GAINED NOTHING\|No test is added\|NOTHING GUARDS THE HARNESS\|the same 396" --include=*.json --include=*.jsonl --include=*.py --include=*.md .` was run FIRST and its four hits - all in this checkpoint, at completed[7], completed[8], authority.scope_note and declared_non_coverage[2] - written down as the list to work through. THAT SWEEP WAS NARROWER THAN THIS BULLET FIRST CLAIMED, AND THE GAP IS THE POINT. It enumerated the TEST-COUNT phrasings and nothing else, so it found and fixed all four of those - and left the SIZE sentences, which fix round 1's own twelve docstring lines had just falsified in the same commit, standing in three places until the final review measured them. That is the exact N-1-of-N shape this checkpoint's own recovery.stop_if names, committed by the bullet claiming to have avoided it. WHAT WAS MISSING IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE RULE: the enumeration owed is not only of the claim you set out to change, but of every number and every sentence your edit could falsify - here, a docstring edit falsifying a line count of the file it sits in. Four packages in a row before this one shipped a correction applied to N-1 of N places; the fix is to enumerate before editing, every time, to enumerate the consequences and not only the subject, and to check the list against the diff at the end rather than re-grepping and hoping.

THE NUMBER THAT MOVED THREE TIMES IS THE ONE NOBODY RE-READ. control_harness.py was 258 lines when the saving was first written down, 270 after fix round 1 added twelve docstring lines, and 276 after the final wave added six more - and the records said 24 throughout, until the final review measured it. Every edit was prose; none of them touched a line of code; each of them falsified a number in three places. A COUNT OF A FILE THAT THE SAME COMMIT EDITS IS THE EASIEST SENTENCE IN A RECORD TO LEAVE STALE, because the edit does not look like it changes anything. The rule this repository already had - re-measure a count after the last edit in the same commit - was written for a population the commit joins; it applies just as hard to a file the commit merely adds prose to.

TWO OF THE FOUR FINAL-WAVE ITEMS ARE THE SAME DEFECT IN DIFFERENT CLOTHES: a sentence that describes what the code happens to do rather than what it guarantees. fresh()'s docstring promised no `.git` while the code only inherited it from its callers, and the guard's docstring promised `wp1??` covered every runner while the pattern stops at wp199. Both read as contracts and neither was one. The repair in both cases was to make the code do what the sentence said, not to soften the sentence.
assumptions: That a difference which changes only an AssertionError message no green run prints - `edit`'s 60-against-70 preview width - is still worth a parameter rather than a unification. The bar this package was set is whole-output equality, and under a fault the two messages differ; keeping the parameter costs one keyword argument and removes the need to argue that the fault path does not count. A reviewer who thinks that is over-cautious is disagreeing with a specific row of the table rather than with the extraction.

That the two `run_validator` shapes are a question with two right answers rather than a divergence to resolve. wp112 and wp114 parse ONE anchored STATE_RECONCILIATION= line out of stdout; wp115 searches stdout and stderr joined for a different string entirely. Only the subprocess call is shared, as run_script. If a reviewer reads these as one function that drifted, the repair is not to unify the return values - it is to say which of the two readings each caller needs, which is what the current split already records.

That leaving `check_source_main_line` in both runners is right. Its two docstrings record two different measurements made at two different times about the same guard, and its behaviour is stated as something this package must not alter. The duplication is real and is declared rather than removed.

authority.scope_note: One new module under scripts/ holding the part of the six negative-control runners that measurement showed is genuinely common, and the six runners rewritten to call it. No runner's behaviour changes; each was proven unchanged by whole-output comparison before and after. Fix round 1 adds ONE test module and ONE runner: tests/test_harness_parameters.py, which reads the harness and the runners as source text and holds the property the extraction rests on, and scripts/wp117_controls.py, which demonstrates that guard can fail. Nothing under tests/ imports the harness and nothing new under tests/ starts a process. No existing test is edited or removed and no runner is wired into CI. AGENTS.md, docs/ and every design are untouched. badf/ and sessions/ are re-anchored and nothing more.

stop_if: A divergence between two runners is resolved by taking the union of the two behaviours, or the more lenient of them, instead of by a parameter with a live caller on each side. That is exactly what WP-110 did to four private normalisers: the suite passed, four re-run controls passed, and review then found eight real divergences that had been caught before the change and were missed after it. A question can have two right answers, one per caller.

A runner is migrated on the strength of the test suite staying green. The suite does not run these files; it cannot tell you a control stopped tripping the test it names. The only evidence that a migration is behaviour-preserving is the runner's OWN whole output, captured before and after and diffed - every control, the test each trips, and every isolation declaration.

A before/after comparison is made over a tree whose badf/ records have been rolled in between. wp112's controls read active_work_package and baseline_commit out of badf/current-state.json, so re-anchoring the package inside the comparison window changes the subject and the diff stops measuring the code change. Capture both sides with badf/ untouched, then roll.

check_source_main_line is deleted, weakened, or shared between wp112 and wp114 by merging their docstrings. It refuses to run when the source checkout's local `main` carries commits its `origin/main` does not, and it exists because an accident once made every clone-based control red for a reason unrelated to the code. One direction only: AHEAD is refused, BEHIND is allowed, and widening it to both was already measured as a false failure and repaired once.

wp112's `the same later merge with the corroboration required to be the TIP` control reporting differently from one run to the next is treated as a regression in whatever change is in flight. It is open defect #360: that control's fixture is synthesised on the clone's tip, so its verdict depends on whether the source checkout's local main has been pulled. Check the source's refs before blaming the code.

A sentence in these files is written without a command that measures it. Every finding across the review rounds on this repository was a sentence that did not match a measurement, and this package's own first act was finding that the issue's headline table did not reproduce.

Anything under tests/ imports scripts/control_harness.py, or a fifth module under tests/ starts calling a subprocess. The suite is offline and subprocess-free apart from four declared modules, measured with `grep -lnE "subprocess[.](run|Popen|check_output|check_call)" tests/*.py`; the bare-word grep returns more and is the wrong filter.

A runner is wired into CI as part of a refactor. #368 records why they are out - a fresh copy or clone per control, and most then run the whole suite over it - and putting them in is a separate change with its own review.

resume_decision, primary_next_action_id, stop_reason or any key under badf/current-state.json's authority block is changed, or a new authority key is minted and then cited. A package that mints one and cites it passes every check, which is open defect #364.

declared_non_coverage: wp112 EXITS 1 ON BOTH SIDES OF ITS COMPARISON and this package does not repair that. One of its nineteen controls is BAD before the change and BAD after it, identically; the diff is empty, which is the property this package was required to demonstrate, but the runner is not green and was not green before. The cause is open defect #360 and the fix is somebody else's. What this means for a reviewer: wp112's migration is proven to change nothing, and is NOT proven over a run in which every control behaves as declared, because no such run was available on this checkout.

check_source_main_line IS NOT EXTRACTED, and the duplication is left standing rather than removed. wp112's and wp114's copies differ in one edge case - wp114 routes the ancestor question through its own `ancestry()` helper, which raises when `merge-base --is-ancestor` returns an exit code other than 0 or 1, where wp112 inlines the subprocess and lets any other code fall through to the refusal - and in their docstrings, which record two different measurements. Neither difference is repaired here and no test covers either.

THE GUARD HOLDS THE SHAPE, NOT THE MEANING, AND THREE THINGS ARE STILL UNGUARDED. tests/test_harness_parameters.py (fix round 1) refuses a defaulted parameter no runner dissents from, which is the property WP-110's failure would re-enter through. It does NOT ask whether a difference is real: two callers passing two values that make no difference to behaviour satisfy it, and whether a divergence is need or drift is the prose classification in the harness's own docstring, which no test reads. It compares dissent as SOURCE TEXT rather than as a value - `ignore=IGNORE` differs from `COPY_IGNORE` because the strings differ, and evaluating them would mean importing the harness - so a caller passing a name that happens to hold the default would be counted as dissenting and would be wrong. And nothing stops a seventh runner being written by copying wp116 instead of importing the harness; that would be caught by review or not at all. Building more than this means deciding whether these runners belong in CI, which #368 explicitly puts outside this change.

THE OUTPUT-EQUALITY PROOF IS A PROOF ABOUT ONE TREE AT ONE COMMIT, NOT ABOUT THE FUNCTIONS. Each runner was compared over the same source checkout at f34891a. That shows the migration did not change what these controls report about THIS tree; it does not show that the parameterised harness is equivalent to the six originals over every possible tree. In particular no comparison exercised `edit`'s AssertionError path, since no control's fixture failed to match, so the preview-width parameter is carried on reasoning rather than on a measurement.

NO RUNNER'S CONTROLS WERE READ FOR CORRECTNESS. This package moved code and proved the reports did not change; it did not ask whether any control is measuring the right thing, whether a DECLARED HOLE is still a hole, or whether a NOT ISOLATED declaration is still true of the tree. A control whose verdict was already wrong before this change is still wrong after it, and the diff would show nothing.

THE LINE-COUNT SAVING IS SIX LINES AND IS NOT AN ARGUMENT FOR THE PACKAGE. Six runners fall from 2,943 to 2,661 lines and the harness is 276, so the same seven files carry 2,937. Counting the two files the branch adds - scripts/wp117_controls.py 208 and tests/test_harness_parameters.py 289, 497 between them - the tree finishes 491 lines LARGER than it started, 2,943 to 3,434. IF THE CASE FOR THIS CHANGE IS MEASURED IN DUPLICATION REMOVED, THERE IS NO CASE; the case is the single reporting loop in place of six that had already drifted, the written classification of every remaining difference, and the guard that holds it. This bullet exists so the saving is not overstated, and it overstated it by 4x until the final review caught it: it said 24 while the tree said 6, because the number was written once and never re-measured after two rounds of docstring edits to the very file it counts. Re-measure a count after the last edit in the same commit, including the edits that only add prose.

FIX ROUND 1 DID NOT RE-RUN THE TWO CLONE-BASED RUNNERS, AND THE REASON IS NOT CONVENIENCE. Between the equality proof and fix round 1 the source checkout's local `main` moved - a stray commit landed there and was then repaired to f34891a, where the proof runs had found 67deeb2. A clone's `origin/main` IS the source's local `main`, so wp112 and wp114 would now be measuring a different subject than either side of the comparison did, and a green or red result would say nothing about fix round 1. Their before/after captures were taken at 03:05-03:10 under identical refs on both sides and stand; nothing after that re-measures them. wp114's printed MEASUREMENT line would also have moved on its own, from `8 mention the word` to 9, because the new guard module mentions `subprocess` in its docstring while calling none.

NO CONTROL EXERCISES THE GUARD'S FLOOR. test_the_harness_exposes_defaulted_parameters refuses a harness with no defaulted parameter at all, so the checks below it cannot pass over an empty set; no control in scripts/wp117_controls.py deletes every default to watch it fire. It is a floor and not an equality on purpose - the harness may gain or lose a parameter without this guard being edited - and it is the one check in the module that is reasoned rather than measured.
